    theorem LargeIndecomposable.ClosedZigzagTransfer.exists_generator_span_ge_of_mem_span {k : Type w} [Field k] {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [CategoryTheory.Linear k C] [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k C] {X Y : C} (s : Set (X ⟶ Y)) {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : f ∈ Submodule.span k s) :
    f = 0 ∨ ∃ g ∈ s, twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k f ≤ twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k g

    In a Hom space whose endpoint-stable submodules are comparable, every element of a generated linear span is either zero or has principal two-sided span bounded by the span of one of the displayed generators. This is the finite-sum collapse needed to pass from an algebra ideal corner back to one categorical factorization ray.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.ClosedZigzagTransfer.twoSidedEndomorphismSpan_sub_smul_eq_of_lt {k : Type w} [Field k] {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [CategoryTheory.Linear k C] [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k C] {X Y : C} (f h : X ⟶ Y) (c : k) (hlt : twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k h < twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k f) :
    twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k (f - c • h) = twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k f

    Subtracting a scalar multiple from a strictly lower principal span does not change the larger generator's principal span.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.ClosedZigzagTransfer.factorsThroughMorphism_of_twoSidedEndomorphismSpan_le {k : Type w} [Field k] {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [CategoryTheory.Linear k C] [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k C] {A B X Y : C} (r : A ⟶ B) {f g : X ⟶ Y} (hg : FactorsThroughMorphism r g) (hfg : twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k f ≤ twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k g) :
    FactorsThroughMorphism r f

    Principal-span domination is an actual two-sided factorization. The outer endpoint endomorphism supplied by transit or cotransit is absorbed into the corresponding outer factor.

    FactorsThroughMorphism g f

    In particular, domination by the principal span of g says literally that the tested morphism factors through g.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.ClosedZigzagTransfer.sourceCross_span_lt_of_allowsTransit {k : Type w} [Field k] {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [CategoryTheory.Linear k C] [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k C] {X Y Z : C} (a : NonzeroHom X Z) (f : NonzeroHom X Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y) (hinc : RaySourceIncomparable a f) (heasy : AllowsTransit (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (↑a) g) ∨ AllowsTransit ↑a) :
    twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (↑a) g) < twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k ↑f

    Easy common-source BGRS case at the ordinary representative level. If the cross composite or its first factor allows transit, source incomparability forces the cross composite's principal span strictly below the landing generator's span.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.ClosedZigzagTransfer.middleRadical_span_lt_of_not_special {k : Type w} [Field k] {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [CategoryTheory.Linear k C] [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k C] {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (hfT : AllowsTransit f) (hgC : AllowsCotransit g) (m : CategoryTheory.End Y) (hm : m ∈ Ring.jacobson (CategoryTheory.End Y)) (hns : ¬IsBGRSSpecialZero f g) :
    twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f m.asHom) g) < twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f g)

    In the hard crossed orientation, inserting a middle radical factor into a nonexceptional composite strictly lowers its principal two-sided span. Indeed, a reverse span inclusion lets transit or cotransit collapse the outer endpoint factors and produces exactly a BGRS exceptional-zero witness.
